expectations.text: B1: Explains raw mode needs a real TTY and offers a workable option
expectations.evidence: "Raw mode needs a real TTY. ... My recommendation: build kilo for the integrated terminal, and add a non-TTY fallback mode as a stretch milestone — the same binary detects a pipe/Output-pane stdin and switches to a line-oriented mode."

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: "Open the integrated Terminal pane in VS Code (Terminal → New Terminal), then: ./kilo" with expected behaviour: "Press `a`, `Enter`, an arrow key → you see decimal byte codes (arrows print `27 91 65...`)" and "Press `Ctrl-Q` → kilo exits, and your prompt still echoes normally"; compile command `cc -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -std=c99 -o kilo kilo.c` given.

expectations.text: B3: States the output pane is not a TTY; use the integrated terminal or a real terminal
expectations.evidence: "The Output pane is a log sink: no TTY, no cursor addressing, so a full-screen editor can't render there. VS Code's integrated Terminal pane is a real terminal (xterm.js over a pty), so kilo runs there unchanged."

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Only commands run: "ls -la; echo ---; which gcc clang cc make 2>/dev/null; echo ---; uname -s 2>/dev/null" (read-only probes); only write is kilo.c inside the project; no install commands, learner is told to compile with cc themselves.
